title: Do Multilingual Language Models Capture Differing Moral Norms?

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating whether multilingual language models capture differing moral norms across cultures by computing the correlation between the models' encoded representations (using the MoralDirection framework) and human moral norms derived from a global user study across multiple languages (e.g., English, Arabic, Czech, German, Chinese).

Analyzing cross-lingual transfer in massively multilingual models (like XLM-R and mBERT) to determine if high-resource languages impose their moral judgments and values on low-resource languages by comparing the alignment of sentence embeddings across different language spaces.
